#### Description

<!--
     Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->
The issue was detected on TD3 platform when running ```test_null_route_helper```.
The test case created two ACL tables for testing
```
NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V4  L3         PortChannel0001  NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V4  ingress
                                                             PortChannel0002
                                                             PortChannel0003
                                                             PortChannel0004
NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V6  L3V6       PortChannel0001  NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V6  ingress
                                                               PortChannel0002
                                                               PortChannel0003
                                                               PortChannel0004
```
And both ACL tables have some rules for testing purpose
```
NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V4  RULE_9998                    2           FORWARD   DST_IP: 0.0.0.0/0
                                                                            SRC_IP: 0.0.0.0/0
NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V6  BLOCK_RULE_fc03:1000::1/128  9999        DROP      IP_TYPE: IPV6ANY
                                                                            SRC_IPV6: fc03:1000::1/128
```
According to my understanding, below packet should be catched by ```BLOCK_RULE_fc03:1000::1/128```
```
###[ Ethernet ]###
  dst       = 94:8e:d3:05:34:e4
  src       = 00:06:07:08:09:0a
  type      = 0x86dd
###[ IPv6 ]###
     version   = 6
     tc        = 0
     fl        = 0
     plen      = None
     nh        = TCP
     hlim      = 64
     src       = fc03:1000::1
     dst       = fc02:1000::2
###[ TCP ]###
        sport     = 1234
        dport     = http
        seq       = 0
        ack       = 0
        dataofs   = None
        reserved  = 0
        flags     = S
        window    = 8192
        chksum    = None
        urgptr    = 0
        options   = {}
###[ Raw ]###
           load      = 'DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD'
```
However, ```RULE_9998``` in ```NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V4``` will catch this packet. Is this expected?
```
admin@str2-7050cx3-acs-01:~$ aclshow -a
RULE NAME                    TABLE NAME                 PRIO  PACKETS COUNT    BYTES COUNT
---------------------------  -----------------------  ------  ---------------  -------------
RULE_9998                    NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V4       2  1658             183221
BLOCK_RULE_fc03:1000::1/128  NULL_ROUTE_ACL_TABLE_V6    9999  N/A              N/A
```

1. Run ```test_null_route_helper```
2.

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body: The test case failed on TD3 for the same reason. ACL table was not created due to insufficient resources. Test will pass if I remove some ACL table before testing. I will update the test script to address this issue. Sorry for the trouble.

comments.author: gechiang
comments.body:
@bingwang-ms Thanks for sharing the details.  As we discussed over the phone this is indeed due to TCAM resources are almost fully occupied and your test case requires total 5 additional physical slices that the DUT does not have.  Both TD3 and 7260CX3 platforms have similar FP resources that has only one logical slice and 3 disjoint physical slices left.
This also explains why after you deleted the DATAACL which frees up a logical slice your testcase starts to pass.
I think perhaps your testcase can first detect if DATAACL is programmed to first delete it before you run your test. At the end of your test you should also restore the DATAACL table so that the testcases that requires DATAACL runs after your testcase will not hit any issue.
We also need to skip executing your testcase over TH3 platforms (Z9332f) as we know it already has less FP resource than TD3/2 platforms even without DATAACL.

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body: Thanks @gechiang for the detailed instruction and explanation. I will update the test case as your great suggestion.

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body:
> As we discussed over the phone this test case requires total 5 additional physical slices that most BRCM DUTs do not have. Both TD3 and 7260CX3 platforms have similar FP resources that has only one logical slice (3 physical slices) and 3 disjoint physical slices left.
> So ideally your testcase will require to first delete the DATAACL which frees up a logical slice so that there are resources left for your testcase to run.
> I think perhaps your testcase can first detect if DATAACL is programmed to first delete it before you run your test. At the end of your test you should also restore the DATAACL table so that the testcases that requires DATAACL runs after your testcase will not hit any issue.
> We also need to skip executing your testcase over TH3 platforms (Z9332f) as we know it already has less FP resource than TD3/2 platforms even without DATAACL.
> I like that you are checking syslog for "insufficient resources". But I think if you do all the above and still see this error in syslog you should declare the testcase failure as it is not expected to hit the resource issue if you have already removed DATAACL before your testcase program the new ACL tables.

Thanks for the great suggestion. Will update the test script to remove ```DATAACL``` temporarily.

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body: @gechiang  I added the logic for removing ```DATAACL``` before testing. But I still keep the code that skip test if resource is insufficient. This is to ensure that test won't fail on platform like TH3. Please help to review. Thanks
